auditor_claire: Hi team — for the SOC2/ISO check I need a reproduceable extraction playbook for three scenarios: (1) RBAC change, (2) KMS key rotation, (3) vuln -> incident. Exact CLI/UI steps, canonical S3/GCS object keys, checksum/signature procedure, immutability/retention, and which control IDs each artifact satisfies. Can you make this runnable so I can re-run it during the verification window?

audit-liaison-bot: If owners confirm prefixes I can pre-create placeholders and a verification ticket. @marta.lopez @kevin.chen @derrick_ng

marta.lopez: I own RBAC. Minimal, concrete steps (multi-cloud): collect PR+approvals, infra plan, cloud audit slice, and cluster subject snapshot. Commands I run: 

```bash
# capture terraform plan as JSON
terraform plan -out=tfplan && terraform show -json tfplan > /tmp/tfplan.json

# AWS CloudTrail slice for IAM events (example epoch ms)
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name "/aws/cloudtrail/Redwood" \
  --filter-pattern "CreateUser|DeleteUser|AttachRolePolicy|PutRolePolicy|UpdateAssumeRolePolicy|AddUserToGroup|RemoveUserFromGroup" \
  --start-time 1730000000000 --end-time 1730000360000 > /tmp/aws_iam_events.json

# GCP audit logs for IAM changes
gcloud logging read "protoPayload.methodName:(\"SetIamPolicy\" OR \"roles\")" --project=redwood-prod --start-time=2024-12-26T00:00:00Z --end-time=2024-12-26T01:00:00Z --format=json > /tmp/gcp_iam_events.json

# Azure AD activity log export (example)
az monitor activity-log list --offset 60m --resource-group Redwood-RG --output json > /tmp/azure_activity.json

# k8s RBAC snapshot
kubectl get rolebinding,clusterrolebinding -o yaml --all-namespaces > /tmp/rolebindings.yaml
kubectl get sa --all-namespaces -o yaml > /tmp/serviceaccounts.yaml
```

marta.lopez: Canonical upload layout (RBAC): s3://audit-exports/rbac/{ticket_id}/{ts}/tfplan.json, aws_iam_events.json, gcp_iam_events.json, azure_activity.json, rolebindings.yaml, serviceaccounts.yaml, approvals.pdf, manifest.txt. We sign manifest with cosign (preferred) and also provide a GPG detach-sign for legacy verification. Example manifest creation + signing: 

```bash
# produce checksums
sha256sum /tmp/tfplan.json /tmp/aws_iam_events.json /tmp/gcp_iam_events.json /tmp/rolebindings.yaml > /tmp/manifest.txt

# sign manifest with cosign (timestamped via Rekor tlog)
cosign sign-blob --key k8s://cosign-key-ref /tmp/manifest.txt > /tmp/manifest.txt.sig

# legacy GPG (optional)
gpg --local-user marta@redwood --armor --detach-sign /tmp/manifest.txt

# upload
aws s3 cp /tmp/tfplan.json s3://audit-exports/rbac/$TICKET/$TS/tfplan.json
aws s3 cp /tmp/manifest.txt s3://audit-exports/rbac/$TICKET/$TS/manifest.txt
aws s3 cp /tmp/manifest.txt.sig s3://audit-exports/rbac/$TICKET/$TS/manifest.txt.sig
aws s3 cp /tmp/manifest.txt.asc s3://audit-exports/rbac/$TICKET/$TS/manifest.txt.asc
# set object metadata (uploader, ci_run)
```

marta.lopez: Control mapping (examples): SOC2 CC6.1 (change management evidence), ISO 27001 A.9.2.3 (user access provisioning audit trail). Retention: hot S3 365 days, archive to Glacier Deep 7 years; finalized bundles get S3 Object Lock (GOVERNANCE). Raw Slack or PII not included in RBAC bundles.

kevin.chen: I own KMS/key lifecycle. We prefer to include both provider metadata + policy + rotation events + envelope usage. Minimal commands (AWS, GCP, Azure examples): 

```bash
# AWS KMS
aws kms describe-key --key-id alias/prod-encrypt > /tmp/aws_key_meta.json
aws kms get-key-policy --key-id alias/prod-encrypt --policy-name default > /tmp/aws_key_policy.json
aws logs filter-log-events --log-group-name "/aws/cloudtrail/Redwood" --filter-pattern "CreateKey|RotateKey|DisableKey|RevokeGrant|CreateGrant|ScheduleKeyDeletion" --start-time 1730000000000 --end-time 1730000360000 > /tmp/aws_kms_events.json

# GCP KMS
gcloud kms keys describe prod-key --location=global --keyring=prod-ring --format=json > /tmp/gcp_key_meta.json
gcloud logging read "resource.type=\"kms_key\" AND protoPayload.methodName:(\"cryptoKeyVersions\" OR \"update\")" --format=json --limit 1000 > /tmp/gcp_kms_events.json

# Azure KeyVault
az keyvault key show --vault-name prod-kv --name prodKey --output json > /tmp/az_key_meta.json
az monitor activity-log list --resource-group Prod-Vault-RG --output json > /tmp/az_kv_events.json

# envelope evidence (example: S3 object with encryption context)
aws s3api head-object --bucket prod-backups --key backups/2024/12/enc-0001.tar.gz > /tmp/object_meta.json
```

kevin.chen: Upload layout (KMS): s3://audit-exports/kms/{provider}/{key_alias}/{ts}/key_meta.json, key_policy.json, kms_events.json, object_meta.json, manifest.txt, manifest.txt.sig. We encrypt the final bundle with the CMK (server-side encryption) and record key_arn. For tamper-evidence we timestamp the cosign signature into Rekor and include the Rekor entry in the bundle.

kevin.chen: Control mapping: SOC2 CC6.2 (cryptographic key lifecycle), ISO 27001 A.10.1 (cryptographic controls). Retention/immutability: same S3 policy + Object Lock; keep key_policy snapshots for the full 7 years.

derrick_ng: For vuln -> incident chain: minimal reproducible dataset = scanner output, triage notes, ticket timeline, PR(s), CI artifact SHA, deploy trace, monitoring alerts, redacted chat transcript. Steps I use: 

```bash
# ticket export (Jira)
curl -s -u $JIRA_API_TOKEN "https://redwood.atlassian.net/rest/api/3/issue/$TICKET" > /tmp/ticket.json

# scanner output (example)
cp /var/tmp/scans/$SCAN_ID.json /tmp/scan.json

# PRs and commits: include shortlog
git --no-pager log --format=\"%H %an %s\" $PR_COMMIT_RANGE > /tmp/pr_commits.txt

# CI artifact hash
sha256sum /workspace/builds/$BUILD/artifact.tar.gz > /tmp/artifact.sha256

# deploy trace
curl -s "https://deploy.internal/api/v1/deploys/$DEPLOY_ID/trace" > /tmp/deploy_trace.json

# monitoring alert snapshot (prometheus)
curl -g "https://prometheus.internal/api/v1/query_range?query=ALERTS&start=$START&end=$END" > /tmp/alerts.json

# slack export + redact
/compliance/export_slack --channel incident-bridge --start $START --end $END > /tmp/slack_raw.txt
python3 /tools/redact_slack.py /tmp/slack_raw.txt /tmp/slack_redacted.txt
```

derrick_ng: Upload path: s3://audit-exports/incidents/{ticket_id}/{ts}/ticket.json, scan.json, pr_commits.txt, artifact.sha256, deploy_trace.json, alerts.json, slack_redacted.txt, manifest.txt, manifest.txt.sig. Mapping: SOC2 CC7.1 (incident response evidence), ISO 27001 A.16.1.3. Chain-of-custody: uploader CI run ID and human reviewer are recorded in object metadata; manifest signed with cosign and timestamped into Rekor. If auditor cannot reach Rekor, we include the tlog entry blob in the bundle to verify later.

auditor_claire: Good detail. Two clarifications: 1) How do you verify cosign signatures locally? 2) Where do I find the public verification keys/fingerprints? Also I need one sample RBAC bundle and one KMS bundle uploaded with exact S3 keys and both cosign sig + legacy gpg signature so I can verify both paths.

marta.lopez: Verification steps we provide in README in each bundle: 

```bash
# download manifest + signature
aws s3 cp s3://audit-exports/rbac/TKT-2026-01/1730000000/manifest.txt ./
aws s3 cp s3://audit-exports/rbac/TKT-2026-01/1730000000/manifest.txt.sig ./

# verify checksums
sha256sum -c manifest.txt

# verify cosign sig (requires cosign configured with our public key)
cosign verify-blob --key https://keys.redwood.internal/cosign.pub --signature manifest.txt.sig manifest.txt

# (alternative) verify GPG
aws s3 cp s3://audit-exports/rbac/TKT-2026-01/1730000000/manifest.txt.asc ./
gpg --verify manifest.txt.asc manifest.txt
```

marta.lopez: Public keys published at https://keys.redwood.internal/ with fingerprints in the README. We also include Rekor entry JSON at s3://audit-exports/rekor-entries/{bundle_id}.json for offline verification.

kevin.chen: For KMS bundles we'll include CMK ARN used to encrypt the bundle and an exported key policy JSON. If the auditor wants to check decryptability we can provide a temporary JIT role with a one-time access token recorded in the ticket (audit-only).

audit-liaison-bot: OK — creating task AUD-2026-1245 and reserving verification window 2026-04-28 14:00 UTC. Please attach one RBAC sample and one KMS sample under s3://audit-exports/samples/ and add README.md with the exact verification commands and key locations.

auditor_claire: Thanks — please ping here when samples are uploaded and include the manifest.sig and manifest.txt.asc so I can test both cosign + gpg verification flows. :white_check_mark:
